title: Parallel and perpendicular lines
keyIdea: A horizontal line lies flat, like the ground, and a vertical line goes straight up and down. Parallel lines go the same way and keep the same gap all along, so they never meet. Perpendicular lines meet or cross at a right angle, a square corner. Length and tilt do not matter: two slanted lines can be parallel, and two slanted lines can be perpendicular.
familyTip: On a walk or at home, hunt for pairs of lines: rails and fence posts for parallel, window corners and table legs on the floor for perpendicular. Ask: do they go the same way, or meet in a square corner?

visual.caption: Parallel or perpendicular? Drag each pair of lines into a box, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: the two rails of a train track
the two strokes of a plus sign +
the two side edges of a door
the two strokes of the letter L

lab.caption: Flagship lab: turn lines to flat, upright, parallel and square-cornered, pick true parallel pairs, sort letters and draw both on a dot grid.

kid: A horizontal line lies flat, like the floor or the top of a table. A vertical line goes straight up and down, like a flagpole. Lines that are not flat or straight up are slanted.

Two lines are parallel if they go the same way. The gap between them is the same all along, so they never meet. Train rails are parallel. Parallel lines can be long or short, and flat, upright or slanted.
Two lines are perpendicular if they meet in a square corner. That corner is a right angle. The corner of a book shows it. The lines can both be slanted, as long as the corner is square.
Be careful with lines that do not touch on the page. If the gap gets smaller, they would meet if you drew them longer. So they are not parallel.
adult: Ages 7 to 8. This matches Year 3 Geometry in the National Curriculum in England (identify horizontal and vertical lines and pairs of perpendicular and parallel lines) and CCSS 4.G.1 (draw and identify perpendicular and parallel lines). It builds on right angles as a quarter turn and leads into the properties of 2-D shapes, such as a rectangle having two pairs of parallel sides and four right angles.

Horizontal and vertical describe one line compared with the ground. Parallel and perpendicular describe a pair of lines compared with each other. Parallel lines keep a constant distance apart and never meet. Perpendicular lines meet at a right angle. Neither idea depends on how long the lines are or on which way the page is turned.

Common mistakes: thinking parallel lines must be the same length, or must be flat. Calling two lines parallel because they do not touch on the page, even though the gap is closing. Thinking perpendicular means one flat line and one upright line, so a tilted square corner is missed. And mixing up the two words.

In the lab your child turns a stick until it is flat and then upright. Next they turn line B until its gap to line A is the same at both ends; dashed lines show where tilted lines would meet. They pick the true parallel pairs from look-alikes and turn a line to make a square corner with a slanted line. Then they sort the letters T, Z, H, V and N, and draw a parallel and a perpendicular line on a dot grid.

practice.prompt: The two rails of a train track never meet and stay the same distance apart. The rails are…
practice.hint: Do the rails go the same way, or meet in a square corner?
practice.explain: The rails go the same way and keep the same gap, so they are parallel. Vertical describes one line going straight up.

practice.prompt: Two parallel lines are {a} cm apart at one end. How many centimetres apart are they at the other end?
practice.hint: What stays the same all along a pair of parallel lines?
practice.explain: Parallel lines keep the same gap all along, so they are {a} cm apart at the other end too.

practice.prompt: On a dot grid, line A goes {a} dots across for every 1 dot up. You draw a parallel line. How many dots across does it go for every 1 dot up?
practice.hint: A parallel line goes the same way, so it copies the steps.
practice.explain: A parallel line copies the steps of line A: {a} dots across for every 1 dot up.

practice.prompt: Line A is slanted. Line B crosses it and makes a square corner. Which is true?
choices: They cannot be perpendicular because A is slanted
practice.hint: What makes two lines perpendicular: their tilt, or the corner they make?
practice.explain: A square corner is a right angle, so A and B are perpendicular. Perpendicular lines can both be slanted.

practice.prompt: Mia says two lines are parallel because they do not touch on the page. But the gap between them gets smaller. Is she right?
choices: No, if they were longer they would meet
Yes, if they are the same length
practice.explain: The gap is shrinking, so longer lines would meet. Parallel lines keep the same gap and never meet.

pool.hint: Where the top bar meets the stem, is the corner square?
pool.explain: The top of T meets the stem in square corners, so the lines are perpendicular. T has no pair of lines going the same way.

pool.prompt: How many pairs of parallel sides does a rectangle have?
pool.hint: Look at the top and bottom, then the two sides.
pool.explain: The top and bottom are parallel, and the left and right sides are parallel. That is 2 pairs.

pool.prompt: On a dot grid, line A goes {a} dots across and 1 dot up. A perpendicular line goes 1 dot across. How many dots down does it go?
pool.hint: A perpendicular line turns the steps round: the across and up numbers swap.
pool.explain: Turning A's steps gives 1 across and {a} down, so the new line meets A in a square corner.

pool.prompt: A flagpole stands straight up from flat ground. The pole is…
pool.hint: Is it flat, or straight up and down?
pool.explain: Straight up and down is vertical. Parallel describes a pair of lines, not one pole.

pool.prompt: A short line and a long line both lie flat, one above the other. Are they parallel?
choices: Yes, they go the same way
No, they are not the same length
pool.hint: Does length change which way a line goes?
pool.explain: Both go the same way, so the gap stays the same. Length does not matter for parallel lines.

pool.prompt: Which letter has a pair of parallel lines but no right angle?
pool.hint: Look for two strokes going the same way, with no square corner.
pool.explain: N has two parallel uprights, and its slant meets them at sharp corners, not right angles. L has a right angle; V has no parallel lines.

pool.prompt: A picture of a fence post is turned on its side. In the turned picture, the post is…
pool.hint: Horizontal and vertical compare a line with the ground at the bottom of the page.
pool.explain: Turned on its side, the post now lies flat on the page, so it is horizontal. The names depend on which way the line points.

pool.prompt: The rungs of a ladder go across between its two long sides. Each rung is…
choices: perpendicular to the sides and parallel to the other rungs
neither parallel nor perpendicular to anything
pool.hint: Look at the corner where a rung meets a side, then compare two rungs.
pool.explain: A rung meets each side in a square corner, so it is perpendicular to the sides. All the rungs go the same way, so they are parallel to each other.

pool.prompt: On a dot grid, line A goes 1 dot across and {a} dots up. A parallel line goes 2 dots across. How many dots up does it go?
pool.hint: A parallel line keeps the same steps. Two lots of 1 across need two lots of the up steps.
pool.explain: Each 1 dot across goes with {a} dots up, so 2 dots across go with {=2*a} dots up. The line goes the same way as A.
